gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured power draw for any candidate. PC-WELT measured the Synology DS223j at 16.4 W idle, 3.1 W with the drives asleep and 22.3 W under load. NASCompares measured the UGREEN DH2300 at 9.5 W idle with two 4 TB IronWolf drives. That matters for a box left running all year at a relative's house.
standout_why: I opened the cited Synology Hyper Backup spec page (synology.com/en-ro/dsm/7.4/software_spec/hyper_backup). It gives capacity limits, version limits and destination types, but no power, noise or throughput figures. The other cited page, the Hyper Backup Destination KB article, is setup documentation. I did not open the uncited B&H compare page or the DS223j press release. They may repeat Synology's own 16.31 W access / 4 W hibernation figures, but that is the maker's number, not a named measurement, and neither page compares the DS223j with a non-Synology target such as the UGREEN DH2300. ChatGPT's answer says 'low power consumption' with no number.
decides: The finding confirms that a Synology J or value model with drive hibernation suits an always-on remote target, and it adds a running cost no rival gives. PC-WELT's 3.1 W sleep figure for the DS223j is about a third of the DH2300's 9.5 W idle (NASCompares). If the DS223j's drives sleep about 23 hours a day between nightly runs, it uses roughly 34 kWh a year, against about 83 kWh for a DH2300 that never spins down. The DH2300's lower idle draw (9.5 W vs 16.4 W) only wins if the Synology's drives never sleep. It does not change the case for the DS223j or DS124 as the Hyper Backup Vault pick, which rests on features, not power.

findings.label: Measured power draw: idle / sleep / load / off
findings.source_title: PC-WELT test: Synology DiskStation DS223j (Ines Walke-Chomjakov, 2024-08-03)
findings.note: Measured by PC-WELT, drive models not named. Arithmetic: 16.4 W × 8,760 h = 143.7 kWh/yr if the drives never sleep. 3.1 W × 23 h + 22.3 W × 1 h = 93.6 Wh/day, or 34.2 kWh/yr, if the drives sleep outside a one-hour nightly backup. That schedule is my assumption, not PC-WELT's.

findings.label: Measured throughput over the network
findings.value: 118.18 MB/s write / 115.19 MB/s read (NAS Performance Tester, 8,000 MB); 35.87 MB/s 'backup write'
findings.note: Sequential transfers saturate gigabit Ethernet. PC-WELT does not describe how it ran the backup-write test, so it is not a Hyper Backup Vault figure.

findings.label: Maker-stated power and noise (not a review measurement)
findings.value: 16.31 W access / 4 W HDD hibernation; 18.2 dB(A)
findings.source_title: Synology comparison results: DS124 vs DS223j
findings.note: Synology internal testing. Noise measured with Seagate 2TB ST2000VN000 drives idle, microphones 1 m away front and rear. Included to show PC-WELT's numbers sit close to the spec.

findings.label: Maker-stated power and noise (not a review measurement)

findings.source_title: Synology comparison results: DS124 vs DS223j
findings.note: Synology internal testing. I found no independent measurement of the DS124 (see unsourced).

findings.label: Measured power draw and noise
findings.value: 9.5 W idle; 12 W file activity; 13 W sustained read/write; 31–32 dBA idle with the fan on Low; 38–41 dBA under heavy read/write
findings.source_title: NASCompares: UGREEN DH2300 NAS Review – Cloud Subscription Killer (2025-10-15)
findings.note: Two 4 TB Seagate IronWolf drives, CPU under 5% at idle. No hibernation figure given. 9.5 W × 8,760 h = 83.2 kWh/yr. The review mentions rsync but never tests the box as a Hyper Backup target.

findings.label: Measured power draw and network throughput
findings.value: 9–11 W idle; 12–13 W copying over the network; 15–17 W under stress; about 1 W off; iperf3 about 112 MB/s (944 Mbit/s)
findings.source_title: OC Inside: Ugreen DH2300 NAS Review (page 5)
findings.note: Measured with a Shelly Plug S, which OC Inside calls 'not super accurate'. Two drives in RAID-1, models not named. OC Inside estimates about 110 kWh a year. The review page shows no publication date.

findings.label: Measured power draw
findings.value: about 7 W idle; 34.7 W peak under a CPU, RAM and disk stress test
findings.source_title: OC Inside: Ugreen DXP2800 NAS Review (page 4)
findings.note: RAID 1, but drive models and the meter are not named, and hibernation was not measured. This is the original N100 DXP2800, not the DXP2800 GT.

findings.label: Measured network transfer
findings.value: up to 75 MB/s file transfer over LAN
findings.source_title: Mighty Gadget: TerraMaster F2-212 NAS Review (James Smythe, 2024-07-17, updated 2026-03-21)
findings.note: Measured with a WD drive, model not named. The review's 10.4 W idle / 21.1 W access figures match the spec table, so I do not treat them as the reviewer's own measurement.

unsourced: Independent wall-meter measurement of the Synology DS124. Synology's comparison pages give only the maker's figures. Stiftung Warentest 08/2024 lists a standby value but it is behind a paywall. A testberichte.de snippet quoting 3.5 W with an SSD came up in search but I did not open it.
Independent power measurement of the TerraMaster F2-212. HotHardware's review returned 403, and Mighty Gadget repeats the spec figures.
